title: lcn starvation forks replicate on fresh seed 4: local food cut kills one cog (<10% by 60 t) and one worm (<10% by 20 t) while neighbours keep their matter; global removal leaves 0.12 of matter after 80 t vs ~1.0 fed
summary: Re-ran the finding's world.py and scripts unchanged on fresh seed 4 (mkcut.py and cutplot.py patched only to take the seed from the command line): pre-run from full-domain noise to t=1000, then from the same checkpoint a fed twin (500 t), a local cut around a median cog (r=18) and around the largest interior worm (r=35), 250 t each, and global removal of food and waste (STARVE_ALL, 500 t). Cog: matter inside the disk below 10% at t=1060, 0.04 at t=1250, against 0.75 in the fed twin; neighbour annulus 1.12 in both arms. Worm: below 10% at t=1020, 0.00 at the end, against 0.72 fed; annulus 0.98 cut vs 1.08 fed. Global: total matter 0.33 at t=1025, 0.14 at 1045, 0.12 from 1085 to 1500 while food regrows to 0.21; the fed twin stays at 0.95-1.17. Labkit pack of seed 4 (t=200): cogs and worms from full-domain noise, 11 final bodies.

observations.E: localcut.png: cut cog <10% at t=1060 (fed 0.75), cut worm <10% at t=1020 (fed 0.72), neighbours 1.12/1.12 and 0.98/1.08; forks_seed4.txt: global removal 0.12 of matter by t~1085 vs fed 0.95-1.17

seeds_run.result: pass: both local cuts kill their body within 20-60 t, neighbours unchanged; global removal leaves 12% of matter

controls_run.E: fed4 (fed twin from the same t=1000 checkpoint) against cutrun_cog4, cutrun_worm4, starve4 (forks_seed4.txt; checkpoints regenerable with runsave.py)

by_construction: E (matter is built only from food)
verdicts.limitation: The worm's cut disk (r=35) also covers several cogs, as the author noted, so the worm row is not a single-body cut. The cog took 60 t to fall below 10%, slower than the finding's 15-45 t, but within the same order. Global removal leaves about 12% of matter alive on regrown food, as on the finding's seeds. One fresh seed.
